evidence: 26 post(s) published in the last 14d, 22 with insights collected; totals over the measured set: likes=0 comments=0 saves=0 reach=71 (mean reach 3.2/post). The harness is producing normally -- renders complete, posts land, the queue holds at target -- so every machine-level check stays green while the RESULT is zero. This is the acceptance counter for the 2026-09-28 GO/PIVOT/KILL gate; a flat engagement read there is this condition, not a starved pipeline. Account reach attribution, newest measured snapshot (09-24 18:23): non-follower=0 follower=6 total=6. Instagram's account insights answer `reach` with `breakdown=follow_type`, so this is the platform's own split, not an inference from a per-post sum: non-follower=0 means nothing outside the follower list was shown these posts at all -- a DISTRIBUTION ceiling rather than a content problem, and the lever the gate's pivot candidate names. Independent witness: Instagram's own account-level counter (accounts_engaged, period=day) read 0 across 9 measured day(s) in this window, so the zero is stated by the platform rather than produced by our collection. Self-closes when a published post is engaged with (any like/comment/save in the window) -- that predicate stays on the per-post columns the gate reads, so a platform counter that disagrees is reported here and never closes it silently.

2026-09-24 18:30Z ops-triage: condition unchanged (22 measured posts, 0 like/comment/save, non-follower reach 0, mean reach 3.2/post) and STILL DELIBERATELY OPEN -- it self-closes on the first engaged published post and it is the counter the 10-05 read is judged against. One root-cause FIX this pass, on the producer side of the whole chain: every cron guard on this board reads a job's CODE (check_weekly_review_gate_wired), its PROMPT text (check_cron_prompt_*), its DELIVERY target (check_cron_delivery) or executions.db for a run that died mid-flight (check_interrupted_run_debris) -- and NOTHING read whether a job still FIRES ('last_run_at' appears in tc_ops.py exactly once, in a comment; zero checks). That is the documented Hermes scheduler gap (a job whose next_run_at sticks in the past while force-run still works, verified 2026-08-04 with 4 consecutive missed ticks) plus its twin, a job that fires and errors every run. Measured cost here: the hourly producer is what renders and tops the publish queue up, so its absence has NO signal of its own -- the queue drains, publishing stops silently at the last clock, and the first alarm is check_queue_runway at the 3-day edge, ~4 days after the stall began. New check_cron_liveness reads the job store's own arming (next_run_at past its slot beyond a 30m grace; failure_streak >= 2), intent-first (a disabled/paused job is a decision, never a stall) and clock-safe (an offset-less stamp is unplaceable, not midnight-UTC). Non-vacuity proven on the live path, not just the pure function: quiet against the real store (checks-audit 62 checks, 1 firing), and against a synthetic stalled store it filed cron-job-stalled with the exact evidence, then AUTO-CLOSED itself when the real store came back. selftest 682 -> 701 assertions, 0 failures.
